## npx
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

Consolidated tools:
- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type
- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck
- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type
- note_create/note_list/note_update/note_delete: Manage notes in notebooks

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dbus - CLI wrapper for op-projection D-Bus objects
#
# Usage:
#   dbus introspect <plugin>            - introspect a plugin object
#   dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]  - introspect a sub-path
#   dbus list                           - list all registered plugin objects
#   dbus get <plugin> [property]        - get property/data from a plugin
#   dbus call <plugin> <method> [args]  - call a method on a plugin
#
# The service is org.opdbus.projection
# Objects live at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>

SERVICE="org.opdbus.projection"
BASE_PATH="/org/opdbus/v1/plugins"

# Normalize plugin name: replace hyphens with underscores
normalize_plugin() {
    echo "${1//-/_}"
}

cmd="${1:-help}"
shift || true

case "$cmd" in
    introspect)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        subpath="${2:-}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        if [[ -n "$subpath" ]]; then
            # Strip leading slash if provided
            subpath="${subpath#/}"
            object_path="${object_path}/${subpath}"
        fi

        exec busctl introspect "$SERVICE" "$object_path"
        ;;

    list)
        echo "Objects registered under $SERVICE:"
        busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null || {
            echo "  (service not running or no objects registered)" >&2
            exit 1
        }
        ;;

    get)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        property="${2:-Data}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus get <plugin> [property]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        iface="org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object"

        exec busctl get-property "$SERVICE" "$object_path" "$iface" "$property"
        ;;

    call)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        method="${2:-}"
        shift 2 || true

        if [[ -z "$plugin" || -z "$method" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus call <plugin> <method> [args...]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        iface="org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object"

        exec busctl call "$SERVICE" "$object_path" "$iface" "$method" "$@"
        ;;

    watch)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            exec busctl monitor "$SERVICE"
        else
            plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
            exec busctl monitor "$SERVICE" --match "path=${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        fi
        ;;

    help|--help|-h)
        cat <<'EOF'
dbus - CLI wrapper for op-projection D-Bus objects

Service:  org.opdbus.projection
Base:     /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>
Interface: org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object

Commands:
  dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]   Show interfaces/methods/properties
  dbus list                            Tree of all registered plugin objects
  dbus get <plugin> [property]         Read a property (default: Data)
  dbus call <plugin> <method> [args]   Call a method on a plugin
  dbus watch [plugin]                  Monitor D-Bus signals (Ctrl-C to stop)

Properties on each plugin object:
  EntityType   - the schema/entity type (e.g. "system.memory")
  EntityId     - unique entity ID
  State        - Valid | Quarantined | Degraded | ...
  Data         - full JSON projection data

Examples:
  dbus introspect keyring
  dbus introspect wireguard interfaces/0
  dbus list
  dbus get keyring
  dbus get keyring State
  dbus watch keyring
EOF
        ;;

    *)
        echo "Unknown command: $cmd" >&2
        echo "Run 'dbus help' for usage." >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dbus - CLI wrapper for op-projection D-Bus objects
#
# Usage:
#   dbus introspect <plugin>            - introspect a plugin object
#   dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]  - introspect a sub-path
#   dbus list                           - list all registered plugin objects
#   dbus get <plugin> [property]        - get property/data from a plugin
#   dbus call <plugin> <method> [args]  - call a method on a plugin
#   dbus watch [plugin]                 - monitor signals

lastPrompt: can introspect list subpaths?

input.new_string:
list|tree)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Objects registered under $SERVICE:"
            busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null || {
                echo "  (service not running or no objects registered)" >&2
                exit 1
            }
        else
            plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")

#   dbus watch [plugin]                 - monitor signals
#
# The service is org.opdbus.projection
# Objects live at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>

SERVICE="org.opdbus.projection"
BASE_PATH="/org/opdbus/v1/plugins"
IFACE="org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object"

# Normalize plugin name: replace hyphens with underscores (canonical form)
normalize_plugin() {
    echo "${1//-/_}"
}

cmd="${1:-help}"
shift || true

case "$cmd" in

        plugin="${1:-}"
        subpath="${2:-}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]" >&2
            exit 1

        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"

            subpath="${subpath#/}"
            object_path="${object_path}/${subpath}"
        fi

        exec busctl introspect "$SERVICE" "$object_path"
        ;;

    list)

        busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null || {
            echo "  (service not running or no objects registered)" >&2
            exit 1
        }
        ;;

        plugin="${1:-}"
        property="${2:-Data}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus get <plugin> [property]" >&2

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")

        method="${2:-}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" || -z "$method" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus call <plugin> <method> [args...]" >&2

shift || true

case "$cmd" in
    introspect)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        subpath="${2:-}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        if [[ -n "$subpath" ]]; then
            subpath="${subpath#/}"
            object_path="${object_path}/${subpath}"
        fi

        exec busctl introspect "$SERVICE" "$object_path"
        ;;

    list|tree)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Objects registered under $SERVICE:"
            busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null || {
                echo "  (service not running or no objects registered)" >&2
                exit 1
            }
        else
            plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
            prefix="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
            busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null \
                | grep "$prefix" \
                | sed "s|${BASE_PATH}/||" \
                || echo "  (no objects found under $prefix)" >&2
        fi
        ;;

    get)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        property="${2:-Data}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus get <plugin> [property]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"

        exec busctl get-property "$SERVICE" "$object_path" "$IFACE" "$property"
        ;;

    call)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        method="${2:-}"
        shift 2 || true

        if [[ -z "$plugin" || -z "$method" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus call <plugin> <method> [args...]" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        object_path="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"

        exec busctl call "$SERVICE" "$object_path" "$IFACE" "$method" "$@"
        ;;

    names)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        subpath="${2:-}"

        if [[ -z "$plugin" || -z "$subpath" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: dbus names <plugin> <subpath>" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
        subpath="${subpath#/}"
        base_object="${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}/${subpath}"

        # Find all direct children of this path
        children=$(busctl tree "$SERVICE" 2>/dev/null \
            | grep -oP "${base_object}/[0-9]+" \
            | sort -u -V)

        if [[ -z "$children" ]]; then
            echo "No children found under $base_object" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        printf "%-6s  %s\n" "INDEX" "NAME"
        while IFS= read -r obj; do
            idx="${obj##*/}"
            raw=$(busctl get-property "$SERVICE" "$obj" "$IFACE" Data 2>/dev/null)
            name=$(echo "$raw" | grep -oP '(?<="id":")[^"]+' | head -1)
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && name=$(echo "$raw" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.read().split('s \"',1)[1].rsplit('\"',1)[0].replace('\\\\\"','\"')); print(d.get('value',{}).get('id',''))" 2>/dev/null)
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && name="(no id field)"
            printf "%-6s  %s\n" "$idx" "$name"
        done <<< "$children"
        ;;

    watch)
        plugin="${1:-}"
        if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then
            exec busctl monitor "$SERVICE"
        else
            plugin=$(normalize_plugin "$plugin")
            exec busctl monitor "$SERVICE" --match "path=${BASE_PATH}/${plugin}"
        fi
        ;;

    help|--help|-h)
        cat <<'EOF'
dbus - CLI wrapper for op-projection D-Bus objects

Service:   org.opdbus.projection
Base path: /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>
Interface: org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object

Commands:
  dbus introspect <plugin> [subpath]   Show interfaces / methods / properties
  dbus list                            Tree of all registered plugin objects
  dbus list <plugin>                   Show subpaths under a specific plugin
  dbus get <plugin> [property]         Read a property (default: Data)
  dbus call <plugin> <method> [args]   Call a method on a plugin
  dbus watch [plugin]                  Monitor D-Bus signals (Ctrl-C to stop)

Properties on each plugin object:
  EntityType   the schema/entity type  (e.g. "system.memory")
  EntityId     unique entity ID
  State        Valid | Quarantined | Degraded | ...
  Data         full JSON projection data

Examples:
  dbus introspect keyring
  dbus introspect wireguard interfaces/0
  dbus list
  dbus get keyring
  dbus get keyring State
  dbus watch keyring
EOF
        ;;

    *)
        echo "Unknown command: $cmd" >&2
        echo "Run 'dbus help' for usage." >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

content.content:
# op-s6-systemctl

D-Bus service that maps `systemctl` commands to `s6`/`s6-rc` operations for Artix Linux systems using s6 as the init system.

## Overview

This daemon provides a D-Bus interface (`org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`) that translates traditional systemd commands to their s6 equivalents, enabling compatibility with tools and scripts that expect systemctl-like behavior.

## D-Bus Interface

**Bus Name**: `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`
**Object Path**: `/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`
**Interface**: `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`

## Method Mapping

| Method | systemctl Equivalent | s6 Equivalent | Description |
|--------|---------------------|---------------|-------------|
| `start(service)` | `start <svc>` | `s6-rc -u change <svc>` | Start a service |
| `stop(service)` | `stop <svc>` | `s6-rc -d change <svc>` | Stop a service |
| `restart(service)` | `restart <svc>` | `stop` then `start` | Restart a service |
| `reload(service)` | `reload <svc>` | `s6-svc -h <svc>` | Send SIGHUP for config reload |
| `enable(service)` | `enable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle add default <svc>` | Enable service at boot |
| `disable(service)` | `disable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle delete default <svc>` | Disable service at boot |
| `status(service)` | `status <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Get detailed service status (JSON) |
| `is_active(service)` | `is-active <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Returns "active" or "inactive" |
| `is_enabled(service)` | `is-enabled <svc>` | Check `/etc/s6-rc/default/` | Returns "enabled" or "disabled" |
| `list_units()` | `list-units` | `s6-rc -a list` | List all active units (JSON) |
| `daemon_status()` | N/A | `pgrep s6-svscan` | Returns "running" or "not-available" |

## Method Signatures

```rust
// Start/stop/restart/reload/enable/disable all return (success: bool, message: String)
async fn start(service: &str) -> (bool, String);
async fn stop(service: &str) -> (bool, String);
async fn restart(service: &str) -> (bool, String);
async fn reload(service: &str) -> (bool, String);
async fn enable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);
async fn disable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);

// Status methods return strings
async fn status(service: &str) -> String;        // JSON with ActiveState, SubState, MainPID
async fn is_active(service: &str) -> String;     // "active" or "inactive"
async fn is_enabled(service: &str) -> String;    // "enabled" or "disabled"
async fn list_units() -> String;                // JSON array of service objects
async fn daemon_status() -> String;             // "running" or "not-available"
```

## Status JSON Format

The `status()` method returns JSON in this format:

```json
{
  "name": "nginx",
  "active_state": "active",
  "sub_state": "running",
  "main_pid": 1234,
  "ready": true,
  "up_time": "3600"
}
```

The `list_units()` method returns a JSON array of status objects.

## Error Handling

All methods provide helpful error messages when s6 tools are not available or when operations fail. The service gracefully handles:

- Missing s6 binaries
- Invalid service names
- Permission errors
- Service not found errors

## Building

```bash
cargo build -p op-s6-systemctl
cargo build -p op-s6-systemctl --release
```

## Running

```bash
# Run directly (requires D-Bus system bus access)
sudo ./target/release/op-s6-systemctl

# Or with cargo
sudo cargo run -p op-s6-systemctl
```

## Dependencies

- Artix Linux with s6 init system
- `s6`, `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat` tools
- D-Bus system bus

## Architecture

Following the 3tched Architecture D-Bus-first principles:

- All service operations go through D-Bus methods
- No direct subprocess spawning from clients
- Schema-driven interface with consistent error handling
- Zero-copy shared memory design patterns

## License

Apache-2.0

content.text:
Now I have the full picture. Here's what's fragile and my suggestions:

---

**Why the sled disappears:**

1. **`/dev/shm` is tmpfs** — wiped on every reboot. The sled only gets written when `write_sled_from_wg` is called, which only happens on a new WireGuard handshake (polled every 15s, 3-minute window). If the projection server restarts or the xray service restarts, the sled is gone until the next client handshake arrives.

2. **`watch_wireguard_handshakes` runs inside the Incus container** (`wg-xray`) via `incus exec` — if Incus is slow or the container is restarting, every poll silently fails and the sled never gets refreshed.

3. **The sled watcher uses an in-memory `seen` HashSet** — it loses state on restart, so it re-sees old handshakes only within the 3-minute window. Miss that window and nothing triggers a rewrite.

4. **The new decoy forwarding hop** — traffic now goes: client → Oracle VPS (wg-decoy) → 3tched. The sled is written from the peer pubkey seen at the `wg0` interface inside `wg-xray`, but the decoy tunnel adds a NAT layer. The peer pubkey seen at `wg-xray` may now be the Oracle VPS pubkey, not the client's original pubkey — so identity injection gets the wrong key.

---

**Suggestions to make it robust:**

**1. Persist the last-good sled to a non-shm path as backup**
On write, also copy to `/var/lib/op-identity/sled.dat`. On startup, if `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is missing, restore from backup. Sled survives reboots and restarts.

**2. Rewrite sled on projection server startup unconditionally**
If a valid backup exists and `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is absent, restore immediately — don't wait for a handshake.

**3. Replace the 3-minute handshake window with a last-seen timestamp file**
Persist `last_handshake_pubkey` to `/run/op-identity/last-peer` so restarts don't lose the peer identity.

**4. Fix the decoy forwarding identity problem**
The Oracle VPS needs to forward the original client pubkey as an HTTP header (if using Xray VLESS) or the sled needs to read identity from the decoy tunnel's `wg show wg-decoy peers` instead of the inner `wg0`. What does the decoy forward — raw WG or VLESS?

Found it. Look at `/etc/s6/sv/opdbus/run` line 20:

```sh
/usr/local/bin/op-identity-sled --iface opdbus --refresh --path /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Every time the `opdbus` service restarts, it calls `op-identity-sled --refresh` with `--iface opdbus`.** That rewrites the sled from the `opdbus` WireGuard interface pubkey — not from the client's handshake pubkey. And now with the extra decoy hop, `opdbus` may not have a valid peer, so the sled gets overwritten with a zero/stale key.

Also the `watch_wireguard_handshakes` watches inside `wg-xray` container via `incus exec`. With the decoy forwarding step, the handshake visible at `wg0` inside that container is now from the Oracle VPS, not the client.

thre shouldnt be a backup. Here's the full breakdown of the zero-trust identity pipeline, mapped to the concert analogy throughout.

---

## The Concert Analogy

> You arrive at a venue. You hand your keys to the **valet** (WireGuard). The valet parks your car and gives you a **claim ticket** (session ID). At the door, you exchange the ticket for an **all-access wristband** (the Ghostbridge identity sled). Every backstage door checks the wristband — not your car, not your ticket — just the wristband. Your car (the WireGuard tunnel) never enters the venue.

---

## Stage 1 — The Valet: WireGuard Handshake & Session ID Derivation

**Files:** `crates/op-gateway/src/wireguard_auth.rs:529-633`

When a peer connects over WireGuard, the gateway derives three cryptographic artifacts:

### Session ID (the claim ticket)
```rust
// wireguard_auth.rs:529-540
let input = format!("WG-SESSION-{}-{}", peer_pubkey, Self::current_timestamp());
let session_ids = self.crypto_engine.generate_session_ids_batch(&[input.as_bytes()]);
// → BLAKE2s hash → 128-bit hex string
```
- Input: Curve25519 peer public key + current timestamp
- Algorithm: **SIMD-accelerated BLAKE2s**
- Output: 16-byte hex session ID — the peer's claim ticket

### PSK (stable parking spot number)
```rust
// wireguard_auth.rs:542-593
let salt = b"WG-STABLE-PSK-2024";  // fixed — no timestamp
// Argon2 KDF over peer pubkey
```
Deliberately **does not rotate** — rotating it would lock peers out mid-session, like changing the valet lot number while cars are still parked.

### Session Key (per-visit ephemeral)
```rust
// wireguard_auth.rs:595-633
let server_nonce = self.generate_server_nonce().await?;
// Argon2 + nonce → ephemeral key, rotated per connection
```

### The Session Record (the claim stub kept by the valet)
```rust
// wireguard_auth.rs:200-215
pub struct WireGuardSession {
    pub session_id: String,        // BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp)
    pub peer_pubkey: String,
    pub psk: String,               // stable Argon2
    pub expires_at: u64,           // 1 hour TTL
    pub auth_method: String,       // "wireguard"
    pub key_rotation_count: u32,
    // ...
}
```
Persisted to SQLite (`wireguard_sessions` table) and cached in `DashMap` (no SQL in the hot path).

---

## Stage 2 — The Wristband Printer: IdentitySled

**Files:** `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs`, `crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs`

Once the WireGuard session is established, a **152-byte shared-memory struct** (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`) is stamped — the all-access wristband:

```
IdentitySled layout (repr(C), 152 bytes):
  [ 0.. 32]  wireguard_pubkey    — who you are
  [32.. 40]  mutation_index      — which version of the schema you authenticated against
  [40.. 72]  hashed_footprint    — Blake3(current schema state) — the hologram on the wristband
  [72.. 88]  trace_id            — UUID v4 — your unique wristband serial number
  [88.. 92]  schema_version
  [92..152]  reserved
  [192..208] nextdns_profile     — e.g., "689ec7" — your VIP section access
```

The **footprint** (Blake3 hash of the live schema state) is the hologram — it proves the wristband was issued by tonight's venue, not a forgery from last week's show.

The **trace_id** is the serial number stamped on your wrist — immutable, linked to a Qdrant vector record for full accountability.

### NextDNS Profile (the VIP section pass)
```python
# deploy/nextdns/upsert-rewrite.py
# Profile ID: 689ec7
# Upserts DNS rewrites: dashboard.3tched.com → 10.0.0.1
```
The NextDNS profile ID travels with the identity sled. It tells the DNS layer which routing rules apply to this peer — their section of the venue.

---

## Stage 3 — The Door Scanner: xray Header Injection

**File:** `deploy/incus/privacy-xray-ingress/etc/xray/config.json:47-50`

xray sits at the venue entrance. It reads the wristband (sled) and stamps the metadata onto every gRPC call:

```json
"grpcSettings": {
  "serviceName": "Ghostbridge.StateSync",
  "multiMode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "X-Ghostbridge-Footprint": "<Blake3 footprint hex>",
    "X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID":  "<UUID v4 hex>"
  }
}
```

At this point, **WireGuard is dropped**. The tunnel delivered the peer to the door; the tunnel itself does not go backstage. xray strips the WireGuard framing and forwards a plain gRPC call carrying only the two header stamps. The car stays in the lot.

The NextDNS profile influences DNS resolution at this layer — `selector_ip` routing directs packets to the correct Incus container before they ever reach the gRPC endpoint.

---

## Stage 4 — The Backstage Guard: GhostbridgeInterceptor

**File:** `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs:34-84`

Every gRPC call hits this Tonic middleware on port **18789** before any handler sees it:

```rust
pub fn ghostbridge_interceptor(mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {
    // 1. Wristband must be present
    let footprint_value = req.metadata().get("x-ghostbridge-footprint").cloned();
    let trace_value    = req.metadata().get("x-ghostbridge-trace-id").cloned();

    if footprint_value.is_none() || trace_value.is_none() {
        return Err(Status::unauthenticated(
            "A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled. Connection Dropped.",
        ));
    }

    // 2. Zero-copy mmap read of the live sled (no DB hit, no network hop)
    let (sled_ptr, _mmap) = op_identity::read_sled()?;
    let sled = unsafe { &*sled_ptr };

    // 3. Hologram check — footprint must match tonight's schema state exactly
    let expected_footprint = hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint);
    if request_footprint != expected_footprint {
        return Err(Status::permission_denied(
            "A.N.N.A. Scribe: Temporal Hash Mismatch. Session footprint out of sync.",
        ));
    }

    // 4. Embed trace ID into gRPC extensions for downstream accountability
    req.extensions_mut().insert(trace_val);
    Ok(req)
}
```

**Validity rule:** the sled is live only if `hashed_footprint != [0u8;32]` AND `trace_id != [0u8;16]`. A zero field means the wristband was never properly stamped — instant ejection.

The check is **zero-copy** — the sled lives in `tmpfs` (`/dev/shm`), mmap'd directly into the process. No SQL, no network, no disk. The guard glances at your wrist under UV light in milliseconds.

---

## Stage 5 — Backstage: gRPC Routing to op-dbus

**File:** `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/main.rs:94-105`

Once the interceptor passes the call, it routes to the internal gRPC service:

```
Default: http://10.200.0.2:50051  (op-dbus, inside the privacy network)
```

Subnet assignments per peer come from `schemas/plugin/privacy_routes.json`:

```json
{
  "wireguard_public_key": "P8c9Kjnv4B3r6C4+...",
  "assigned_ip":  "10.100.0.2/32",    // WireGuard tunnel allocation
  "selector_ip":  "10.100.0.2",       // OpenFlow packet-match label
  "container_name": "privacy-route-550e8400"
}
```

OpenFlow matches `selector_ip` and routes to the correct Incus container. The WireGuard subnet (`10.100.0.0/24`) exists only to give each peer a unique identity label — it is never forwarded as a WireGuard packet beyond the gateway.

A Linux user session (`wg-{first12ofpubkey}`) is created via `loginctl enable-linger`, giving the peer a D-Bus session and `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` — the backstage room with their name on the door.

---

## Complete Flow, Annotated

```
[Peer]
  │  WireGuard UDP (Curve25519 handshake)
  ▼
[op-gateway / WireGuard endpoint]
  │  BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp) → session_id        ← claim ticket issued
  │  Argon2(pubkey, stable-salt) → PSK               ← stable parking spot
  │  Argon2(pubkey, nonce)       → session_key        ← tonight's coat check
  │  Write IdentitySled → /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat  ← wristband stamped
  │
  │  WireGuard framing DROPPED here ──────────────────← car stays with valet
  ▼
[xray ingress]
  │  Reads sled: footprint + trace_id + nextdns_profile
  │  Injects gRPC metadata headers:
  │    X-Ghostbridge-Footprint: <blake3-hex>
  │    X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID:  <uuid4-hex>
  │  NextDNS profile → DNS rewrites applied (VIP section routing)
  ▼
[GhostbridgeInterceptor — port 18789]
  │  Header present?    No  → 401 "Connection Dropped"
  │  Footprint matches? No  → 403 "Temporal Hash Mismatch"
  │  Zero-copy mmap sled read (tmpfs, no DB)
  │  Inject trace_id into gRPC extensions
  ▼
[op-dbus gRPC — 10.200.0.2:50051]
  │  Full access to internal services
  │  Trace ID rides every call → Qdrant vector linkage for audit
  ▼
[Incus container — privacy-route-{user_id}]
  └─ Linux user session, D-Bus activated, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR alive
```

---

## Why This Is Genuinely Zero-Trust

| Zero-Trust Principle | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Never trust, always verify | Every gRPC call re-validates the live sled footprint — no cached "logged in" state |
| Verify cryptographic state, not identity claims | Footprint is Blake3 of current schema — a stale wristband from an old schema is invalid |
| Least privilege | NextDNS profile scopes DNS; `assigned_ip/32` scopes the subnet to exactly one peer |
| Full audit trail | Trace ID links every call to a Qdrant vector record — immutable, append-only |
| No implicit trust from network location | Being inside `10.100.0.0/24` grants nothing — the wristband check happens regardless |

The WireGuard subnet is purely a **cryptographic identity label** — it gets the peer through the front door and into the valet system. The moment they're inside, the car (the tunnel) stays parked. Everything backstage runs on the wristband alone.

Yes. The Oracle VPS doesn't need to run a WireGuard server at all. It can be a pure UDP relay — just `iptables` DNAT forwarding the client's WireGuard packets straight through to 3tched, with wgcf as the egress so the source IP is a Cloudflare address:

```

3tched's WireGuard sees the **real client pubkey** because the WireGuard session is never terminated at the Oracle VPS — the handshake flows through transparently. The Oracle VPS is invisible.

```sh
# On Oracle VPS
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1

# Forward incoming WG UDP through wgcf to 3tched
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p udp --dport 51820 \
  -j DNAT --to-destination <3tched-ip>:51820

iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o wgcf -j MASQUERADE
```

This solves the identity problem at the same time — no more Oracle VPS pubkey showing up in `wg show latest-handshakes` on 3tched. The real user's pubkey reaches `wg-xray` directly, `watch_wireguard_handshakes` works as designed, and the sled gets written with the correct identity.

Right — the WireGuard subnet/header drop is xray's normal decapsulation behavior mid-session, not a disconnect event. By the time it happens the sled is already written and headers already injected. content.text:
The containers only have loopback — they're not on any network. That's why domains can't resolve to them.

And the point about Gemma: rather than retooling the routing layer twice (first static rules, then Gemma), wire Gemma in now as the router so there's no rework.

So the plan would be:
1. Connect containers to a reachable network (ovsbr0 or a new bridge)
2. xray forwards all traffic to a single Gemma endpoint via zeroclaw
3. Gemma reads the domain/SNI/headers and routes to the correct container

That way there are no static domain rules to maintain — Gemma handles it dynamically from the start. Want to go that route?

Now I have everything I need. Here is the full analysis:

---

## Current Plugin vs Official Incus API: Gap Analysis

### Fields captured by the current plugin

The `IncusInstance` struct (and matching `RawIncusInstance`) captures:

| Field | In struct | In schema |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | yes |
| `status` | yes | yes |
| `type` / `instance_type` | yes | yes |
| `profiles` | yes | yes |
| `config` | yes | yes |
| `devices` | yes | yes |
| `image` (synthetic, extracted from `config["image.description"]`) | yes | yes |
| `storage_pool` (synthetic, extracted from `devices["root"]["pool"]`) | yes | yes |

---

### Official API fields that are entirely missing

The Incus REST API returns these fields on every `GET /1.0/instances/{name}` (with `recursion=1`) that the current plugin silently discards:

| Official field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture` | string | e.g. `"x86_64"` |
| `description` | string | Human description of the instance |
| `ephemeral` | bool | Delete on shutdown |
| `stateful` | bool | Whether saved state exists on disk |
| `created_at` | RFC3339 datetime | Creation timestamp |
| `last_used_at` | RFC3339 datetime | Last-start timestamp |
| `location` | string | Cluster member name; `"none"` on single-node |
| `project` | string | Incus project name; usually `"default"` |
| `status_code` | integer | Numeric status code (100=Stopped, 103=Running, 110=Frozen) |
| `expanded_config` | object | Config after all profiles are merged |
| `expanded_devices` | object | Devices after all profiles are merged |

The `RawIncusInstance` deserializer will silently drop all of these because serde's `#[serde(default)]` ignores unknown fields.

---

### Proxy device shape in the raw API response

A proxy device appears inside the `devices` object as a named key with `"type": "proxy"`:

```json
"devices": {
  "grpc-socket": {
    "type": "proxy",
    "listen": "unix:/run/incus-grpc.sock",
    "connect": "unix:/run/internal/grpc.sock",
    "bind": "host",
    "uid": "0",
    "gid": "0",
    "mode": "0660"
  }
}
```

The device name (`"grpc-socket"` in the example) is the only stable identifier — it is the natural `id` for a named D-Bus object path. Other important proxy fields: `listen`, `connect`, `bind`, `nat`, `proxy_protocol`, `security.uid`, `security.gid`.

Currently the plugin's `devices` field is a flat `HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>>` — proxy devices are in there but not distinguished from NIC, disk, or other device types, and nothing surfaces them as a dedicated `sockets` array.

---

### Specific gaps to fill

**In `incus.rs` — Rust structs:**

1. Add to `IncusInstance`:
   - `architecture: Option<String>`
   - `description: Option<String>`
   - `ephemeral: Option<bool>`
   - `stateful: Option<bool>`
   - `created_at: Option<String>` (ISO8601)
   - `last_used_at: Option<String>`
   - `location: Option<String>`
   - `project: Option<String>`
   - `sockets: Vec<IncusProxySocket>` — **new computed field, not raw API**

2. Add new `IncusProxySocket` struct:
   ```rust
   pub struct IncusProxySocket {
       pub id: String,          // device name → D-Bus object path segment
       pub listen: String,      // e.g. "unix:/run/foo.sock"
       pub connect: String,     // e.g. "unix:/run/internal/bar.sock"
       pub bind: Option<String>, // "host" or "instance"
       pub uid: Option<String>,
       pub gid: Option<String>,
       pub mode: Option<String>,
   }
   ```

3. Add to `RawIncusInstance`:
   - `architecture`, `description`, `ephemeral`, `stateful`, `created_at`, `last_used_at`, `location`, `project`

4. Update `parse_instance_list` to:
   - Copy new fields from `RawIncusInstance` into `IncusInstance`
   - Extract proxy devices (`device.get("type") == Some("proxy")`) into `sockets: Vec<IncusProxySocket>`, setting `id` from the map key
   - Leave non-proxy devices in `devices`

5. Update `instances_equivalent` to include `sockets`/new fields in the comparison as appropriate (most new fields are read-only from the API and shouldn't be diffed for convergence, but `description`, `ephemeral`, and `stateful` are writable).

**In `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — schema:**

Add to `instance_fields`:

| Field | FieldType | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `architecture` | String | false | read_only: true |
| `description` | String | false | writable |
| `ephemeral` | Bool | false | writable |
| `stateful` | Bool | false | read_only |
| `created_at` | String | false | read_only: true |
| `last_used_at` | String | false | read_only: true |
| `location` | String | false | read_only: true |
| `project` | String | false | read_only_when: Some("after creation") |
| `sockets` | Array(Object) | false | computed from proxy devices; each object has `id`, `listen`, `connect`, `bind`, `uid`, `gid`, `mode` |

The `sockets` array schema object should have `id` as `required: true` with `read_only: false` so the D-Bus layer can route each socket to `/incus/{instance_name}/sockets/{id}`.

---

### Official OpenAPI spec URL

The canonical machine-readable spec is at:
**`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lxc/incus/main/doc/rest-api.yaml`**

The rendered web version is linked from `https://linuxcontainers.org/incus/docs/main/rest-api/` but the actual field-level detail requires the YAML directly.

/// A proxy device exposed as a Unix socket on the host.
/// The `id` field is the Incus device name — used as the D-Bus object path segment.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub struct IncusProxySocket {
    /// Incus device name (e.g. "grpc-socket", "mail-imap") — D-Bus path segment.
    pub id: String,
    /// Host-side listen address (e.g. "unix:/run/assistant.sock")
    pub listen: String,
    /// Container-side connect address (e.g. "tcp:127.0.0.1:50051")
    pub connect: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub bind: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub uid: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub gid: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub mode: Option<String>,
}

    pub status: String,

content.text:
Yes to both:

- **Netmaker reverse proxy** — gone. xray routes `api.sock` → netmaker API, `ui.sock` → netmaker-ui by domain tag
- **MQ** — xray handles it fine. Mosquitto is pure TCP, xray routes via `dokodemo-door` to the sockets:
  - `/run/netmaker/mq.sock` → MQTT `:1883`
  - `/run/netmaker/mqtts.sock` → MQTTS `:8883`
  - `/run/netmaker/mq-ws.sock` → MQTT-over-WebSocket `:9001`

All already have unix sockets on the host. xray just needs outbound tags pointing to those sockets and inbound rules matching the ports/domains.

The netmaker container also has a local forward from `tcp:127.0.0.1:1883` → `unix:/run/netmaker/mq.sock` which looks like netmaker itself connecting to MQ internally — that stays, it's internal to the container.

Want me to draft the xray routing rules for all the sockets we now have?

content.text:
Two important points:

**1. Not all sockets are gRPC** — only some:

| Socket | Protocol |
|---|---|
| `assistant.sock` → `:50051` | gRPC |
| `qdrant.sock` → `:6334` | gRPC |
| `qdrant.sock` → `:6333` | HTTP REST |
| `netmaker/api.sock` → `:8081` | HTTP REST |
| `netmaker/ui.sock` | HTTP |
| `mq.sock` → `:1883` | MQTT (raw TCP) |
| `mqtts.sock` → `:8883` | MQTT TLS |
| `mail-3tched/*.sock` | IMAP/SMTP (raw TCP) |

xray outbound transport needs to match per socket — `grpcSettings` for gRPC, `tcpSettings` for mail/MQTT, `httpSettings` for REST.

**2. D-Bus + OVS first** — we violated this when we ran `incus config device add` directly. Any network/OVS operation should go through `op-openvswitch-daemon` D-Bus, and container config changes through the incus plugin's `apply_state`, not raw CLI.

content.text:
You're right — wrap everything in Tonic gRPC. Then xray is uniform gRPC routing on every socket, reflection gives auto-discovery, tonic-web covers browsers. The underlying protocol (IMAP, SMTP, MQTT, HTTP) becomes an implementation detail behind the gRPC facade.

So the pattern for each service:

```
xray → unix socket → Tonic gRPC adapter → underlying service (IMAP/SMTP/MQTT/HTTP)
```

Each adapter:
- Listens on the unix socket
- Accepts Ghostbridge identity headers
- Exposes gRPC reflection
- Proxies to the real service internally

You already have this for `assistant` (`:50051`) and `qdrant` (`:6334`). The gaps are:

| Service | Needs adapter |
|---|---|
| `mail-3tched` | gRPC → IMAP/SMTP |
| `netmaker` API | gRPC → HTTP REST |
| `netmaker-mq` | gRPC → MQTT (streaming) |
| `netmaker-ui` | gRPC-web → HTTP |

Do you want these as a separate `op-grpc-adapters` crate, or one adapter per service crate?

Add gRPC adapters, s6_systemctl plugin, identity sled fixes, named D-Bus paths

## op-grpc-adapters (new crate)
- Uniform gRPC facade over mail (IMAP/SMTP), netmaker REST, and MQTT
- Tonic-web + gRPC reflection + tonic-health on /run/op-grpc-adapters.sock
- Ghostbridge identity interceptor on all services
- s6 service definition at /etc/s6/sv/op-grpc-adapters/

## op-plugins
- s6_systemctl plugin: projects op-s6-systemctl daemon state + all s6 units
- incus plugin: adds IncusProxySocket, surfaces proxy devices as named sockets
- incus schema: architecture, description, ephemeral, stateful, created_at,
  last_used_at, location, project, sockets fields from official Incus API
- s6 plugin: fallback to direct s6-rc CLI when D-Bus daemon not running
- socket_id_from_connect: well-known port → service name mapping

## op-projection / plugin_reader
- Named D-Bus paths: checks id, name, label, key, path, domain, host fields
  in order — eliminates numeric indexes for all array items across all plugins

## op-identity
- watch_wireguard_handshakes: replaced 15s poll + 3min window with
  ip monitor route inside wg-xray container for instant peer detection

## op-s6-systemctl
- restart method: uses s6 process restart instead of s6-rc stop+start

## bin/dbus
- New CLI wrapper: dbus introspect/list/get/call/watch/names commands
- Routes to org.opdbus.projection /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>

## opdbus s6 service
- Removed incorrect sled writing from opdbus/run — sled is session-bound,
  written by op-gateway at WireGuard handshake time, not by opdbus

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user wanted a series of improvements to the operation-dbus-proto workspace (branch: `consolidated-rejected-branches`):
   - Create a `dbus` CLI wrapper for introspecting D-Bus plugins
   - Make D-Bus projection paths use human-readable names instead of numeric indexes (globally)
   - Create a new `s6_systemctl` state plugin so the op-s6-systemctl daemon gets projected with a UI-renderable schema
   - Fix the identity sled disappearing (caused by `opdbus/run` overwriting it on every restart)
   - Refactor `watch_wireguard_handshakes` from a 15s poll with 3-minute window to event-driven `ip monitor`
   - Enhance the incus plugin with official API fields and surface proxy devices as named `sockets`
   - Create `op-grpc-adapters` crate wrapping mail (IMAP/SMTP), Netmaker REST, and MQTT behind uniform gRPC
   - Deploy, commit, and push all changes

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **D-Bus projection**: org.opdbus.projection service, objects at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>`, interface `org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object`
   - **Identity Sled**: 152-byte `#[repr(C)]` struct at `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`, session-bound tmpfs, written by op-gateway at WireGuard handshake time
   - **Ghostbridge pipeline**: WG handshake → sled written → xray reads sled → injects `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` on ALL WG-originated gRPC traffic
   - **Zero-trust**: footprint = Blake3(pubkey + schema_catalog_hash + mutation_index), validated on every gRPC call via mmap
   - **s6 init system**: Chimera-derived, uses `s6 process`, `s6 live`, `s6 set` commands
   - **Incus containers**: Unix socket proxy devices (type=proxy) expose services on host without IPs
   - **xray tag-based routing**: routes by domain/port tag to unix socket outbounds, no nginx needed
   - **Tonic gRPC**: tonic-web for browser support, gRPC reflection for auto-discovery
   - **Oracle VPS as dumb UDP relay**: DNAT forwards WireGuard UDP transparently so wg-xray sees real client pubkeys
   - **D-Bus first mentality**: all control plane ops must go through D-Bus / op-openvswitch-daemon, not direct CLI
   - **Gemma routing (future)**: Gemma AI available via zeroclaw plugin will handle dynamic routing, not yet introduced

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/bin/dbus`** (NEW)
     - Shell script CLI wrapper for D-Bus plugin introspection
     - Commands: `introspect`, `list`, `get`, `call`, `watch`, `names`, `tree`
     - Service: `org.opdbus.projection`, base path `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins`
     - `dbus names <plugin> <subpath>` reads `Data.value.id` to show human names
     - Symlinked to `~/.local/bin/dbus`

   - **`crates/op-projection/src/plugin_reader.rs`** (MODIFIED)
     - Named D-Bus paths — checks multiple fields in priority order:
     ```rust
     let segment = ["id", "name", "label", "key", "path", "domain", "host"]
         .iter()
         .find_map(|&field| child.get(field).and_then(|v| v.as_str()))
         .map(|s| s.replace(['/', ' ', ':'], "_"))
         .unwrap_or_else(|| index.to_string());
     ```
     - Array items with `id` or `name` fields now get named D-Bus paths globally

   - **`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/s6_systemctl.rs`** (NEW)
     - Projects op-s6-systemctl daemon state and all s6 units
     - `S6SystemctlState`: daemon_running, bus_name, object_path, interface, units
     - `S6UnitStatus`: id (unit name), active_state, sub_state, enabled, main_pid, up_time
     - `probe_daemon()`: checks `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` on system bus

Now I see the issue clearly.
